props.gloss_en: after all, throwing is a tolda of carrying-out
R' Yochanan: [carrying-out is written] as the verse says: 'and Moses commanded and they passed a proclamation in the camp' (Ex 36:6)
where was Moses sitting? in the camp of the Levites, and the camp of the Levites was the public domain
and he was telling Israel: do not carry out and bring from your private domain to the public domain
perhaps he stood [commanding] on a weekday, because the work was complete, as it is written 'and the work was sufficient' (Ex 36:7)
as there [the shofar of Yom Kippur] the passing is on a prohibited day, so here the passing is on a prohibited day
after all, it is from domain to domain -- what difference is it to me whether carrying out or carrying in?
carrying-in [is a prohibited labor]: it is a logical inference
however, carrying-out is an av and carrying-in is a tolda
if he did two avot together, or two toldot together, he is liable twice
and if he did an av and its own tolda, he is liable only once
R' Eliezer, who holds one liable for a tolda in the place of an av

alternatively: that which is written he calls an av, and that which is not written he calls a tolda
the mishna: one who throws four cubits at a wall -- above ten handbreadths, it is like throwing into the air; below ten handbreadths, like throwing onto the ground
and one who throws four cubits onto the ground is liable

rather: for the sewers of the curtains threw their needles to one another
